html:
A wrought iron lattice tower in Paris, built from 1887 to 1889 as the entrance to the World's Fair of 1889. At about 300 metres it was the tallest structure in the world until the Chrysler Building in New York passed it in 1930.

The fair marked a hundred years since the French Revolution. The tower was designed by engineers working for the company of Gustave Eiffel, which had built bridges and the iron frame inside the Statue of Liberty. It is made of some 18,000 iron parts held by millions of rivets, and it was built in about two years.

Many artists and writers signed a protest against the "useless and monstrous" tower. It was meant to stand for only twenty years. It was saved because it proved useful for radio, and its antennas carried military signals in the First World War.

It became the symbol of Paris and of France, and one of the most visited monuments in the world. It also showed what iron and steel could do, a step toward the skyscraper.
